# Adjudication Task — Chapter 917

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃917화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|화아악.
  6|
  7|거센 광풍이 휘몰아친다. 지면에 켜켜이 쌓여 있던 새카만 잿가루가, 아직 꺼지지 않는 불씨가 바람을 타고 온 사방에 흩날렸다.
  8|
  9|그리고 모두의 시야를 차단한 그 희뿌연 장막 속에서, 화염을 머금은 일권(一拳)이 공간을 갈랐다.
 10|
 11|퍼엉, 콰아아아!
 12|
 13|압축된 공기가 터져 나간다. 달구어진 공기 너머로 백색 화염이 넘실거렸다.
 14|
 15|그것은 그 무엇으로도 막을 수 없는 불길이었다.
 16|
 17|용의 숨결이었고, 포효였으며, 가늠할 수 없을 만큼 거대한 분노였다.
 18|
 19|감히 자신의 역린(逆鱗)을 건드린 적들을 향해 쏟아지는 늙은 용의 화염은, 그 어느 때보다 맹렬하게 타올랐다.
 20|
 21|이미 불멸(不滅)에 가까운 존재로 거듭난 누군가가 자신도 모르게 죽음이라는 단어를 떠올릴 만큼.
 22|
 23|‘아.’
 24|
 25|동천마군은 내심 침음성을 흘렸다.
 26|
 27|어느덧 두려움과 경탄이 뒤섞인 회색빛 눈동자는 끊임없이 화염을 쏟아내며 다가오는 한 사람을 향하고 있었다.
 28|
 29|화왕(火王) 적천강.
 30|
 31|바로 그였다.
 32|
 33|오직 그였다.
 34|
 35|저 드높은 하늘에 닿지 못했던 열 명의 왕.
 36|
 37|그중에서도 가장 앞선 불의 제왕(帝王)이 비로소 숨겨 두었던 날개를 펼쳐 솟아오르고 있었다.
 38|
 39|무신이라는 하늘을 장식한 세 개의 별들을 향해.
 40|
 41|건드려서는 안 될 것을 건드린, 자신의 적들을 향한 분노를 토해 내며.
 42|
 43|드드득!
 44|
 45|전신을 두드리는 거대한 충격.
 46|
 47|미증유의 힘이 실린 일장(一掌)에 동천마군의 주위를 빈틈없이 에워싸고 있던 죽음의 기운이 뒤흔들린다.
 48|
 49|만근의 힘으로 지면에 틀어박힌 두 다리가 깊은 고랑을 만들어 내며 밀려났다.
 50|
 51|쾅! 쾅! 콰아앙!
 52|
 53|나아가는 자.
 54|
 55|그리고 물러날 수밖에 없는 자.
 56|
 57|적천강이 전자라면 동천마군은 후자였다.
 58|
 59|마치 신벌(神罰)처럼 쉴 새 없이 떨어지는 벼락을 피해 한껏 몸을 웅크린 죄인이었다.
 60|
 61|‘어떻게, 도대체 어떻게…….’
 62|
 63|이미 크고 작은 상처가 가득한 저 지친 육신으로 어찌 이토록 강한 힘을 낼 수 있단 말인가.
 64|
 65|저토록 분노할 수 있단 말인가.
 66|
 67|동천마군은 혀끝에서 감도는 탄식을 삼켰다.
 68|
 69|그리고 압도적인 기세를 흩뿌리며 다가오는 적천강을, 손을 뻗으면 만져질 것만 같은 그의 극렬한 분노를 이해하는 자신을 발견했다.
 70|
 71|그 또한 마찬가지였으니까.
 72|
 73|쾅!
 74|
 75|가족을 잃고.
 76|
 77|콰앙!
 78|
 79|사문을 잃었다.
 80|
 81|콰아앙!
 82|
 83|그렇게 모든 것을 잃었다고 생각한 그때, 텅 비어 버린 자신의 마음 한구석에 남아있던 무언가를 발견했다.
 84|
 85|‘분노.’
 86|
 87|희로애락(喜怒哀樂)을 느낄 수 있기에 인간이라고 했다.
 88|
 89|웃고, 분노하고, 슬퍼하며, 즐길 수 있기에 생명이라고 했다.
 90|
 91|그러나 동천마군은 그중 셋을 잃어버렸다.
 92|
 93|남아 있는 것이 오직 분노뿐이었기에, 마침내 스스로 인간을 포기한 괴물이 되었다.
 94|
 95|복수귀(復讎鬼)라는 이름의 괴물이.
 96|
 97|그렇기에 한편으로는 적천강을, 생사의 갈림길에 선 제자를 본 늙은 스승의 마음을 이해했다.
 98|
 99|자신이 온 힘을 다해 일으킨 죽음의 기운마저 불사르려 하는 저 강대한 화염에 담긴 분노 역시도.
100|
101|콰아아아앙!
102|
103|그 순간.
104|
105|동천마군은 느낄 수 있었다.
106|
107|그를 둥글게 에워싸고 있던 죽음의 기운이 마침내 한계에 다다랐다는 것을.
108|
109|지금 이 순간만큼은 적천강의 분노가, 자신의 분노를 넘어섰다는 것을.
110|
111|쩌적.
112|
113|균열을 알리는 그 소리가 동천마군의 귓가에 닿았다. 그의 몸 깊숙한 곳에서 끊임없이 흘러나오던 기운이 흩어지고 있었다.
114|
115|그리고 그 균열의 시작점에 새하얀 광염(光焰)이 깃든 주먹이, 최후의 보루를 무너트리는 화염과 그보다 더한 열기를 줄기줄기 쏟아 내는 두 눈동자가 있었다.
116|
117|“똑똑히 깨달아라.”
118|
119|그저 마주한 것만으로도 잿더미가 되어 버릴 듯한 안광.
120|
121|“네놈이 무엇을 건드렸는지.”
122|
123|그러나 흘러나오는 목소리는 북해의 빙하처럼 차갑다. 동천마군의 등골을 얼리고 영혼에 스며들었다.
124|
125|그가 죽음을 딛고 일어선 그날부터 오랫동안 잊고 있던 공포를 깨웠다.
126|
127|‘허.’
128|
129|동천마군은 자신도 모르게 몸을 떨었다. 실소를 흘렸다.
130|
131|그리고 불현듯 깨달았다.
132|
133|‘어쩌면 삼성(三星), 그 이상.’
134|
135|적어도 지금 이 순간만큼은, 늙은 용의 분노를 막을 수 있는 것은 아무것도 없었다.
136|
137|아무것도.
138|
139|콰창!
140|
141|마침내 갈라지고, 깨져 나간다.
142|
143|자신을 둘러싸고 있던 모든 것이 산산이 부서지는 소리와 함께, 동천마군은 시야를 물들이며 쏟아지는 백색 화염을 향해 일권을 내질렀다.
144|
145|후웅!
146|
147|소리보다 앞선 움직임.
148|
149|죽은 자와 산 자의 격돌.
150|
151|새하얗게 물든 세상 속, 느릿하게 나아간 멸염신권(滅炎神拳)이 동천마군의 주먹과 맞닿았다.
152|
153|아니.
154|
155|휩쓸었다.
156|
157|쾅!
158|
159|한순간의 격돌. 거대한 굉음.
160|
161|그러나 두 주먹이 서로를 향해 맞닿은 그 시간은 너무나도 짧았고, 힘의 균형은 이미 기울어져 있었다.
162|
163|콰득.
164|
165|이미 흐트러져 버린 사기(死氣)를 집어삼킨 열기가 살갗을 짓이긴다. 혈도와 힘줄을 녹이고 뼈마디를 부수었다.
166|
167|동천마군이 인간으로서의 삶을 포기하며 얻은, 더욱 강건해진 육체와 회복력 따위는 아무런 소용도 없었다.
168|
169|콰아아아!
170|
171|적천강의 일권은 용암인 동시에 섬광이었다.
172|
173|멸염신권이라는 명칭에 담긴 뜻처럼 그가 일으킨 화염은 모든 것을 잿더미로 멸하며 쏘아졌다.
174|
175|동천마군의 주먹으로도 모자라 그의 한쪽 팔 전체를 집어삼켰다.
176|
177|화륵, 퍼어엉!
178|
179|고점에 다다른 화염이 폭발한다.
180|
181|하지만 마땅히 터져 나와야 할 피도, 그 흔한 살점과 뼛조각조차 찾아볼 수 없었다.
182|
183|모조리 증발하거나 잿더미가 되어 버렸으니까. 시간을 되돌리지 않는 한 두 번 다시 회복시킬 수 없게 사라져 버렸으니까.
184|
185|동천마군은 누구보다 그 사실을 잘 알고 있었고, 그것은 적천강 역시 마찬가지였다.
186|
187|팟.
188|
189|단 한 걸음.
190|
191|적천강이 내디딘 발걸음을 따라 공간이 접혔다.
192|
193|잘못 쏘아진 포탄처럼 뒤로 튕겨 나가던 동천마군이 이를 악물며 신형을 비틀었다.
194|
195|콰득, 쾅!
196|
197|옆구리를 스친, 정확히는 스친 것만으로도 한 뼘이나 되는 살점과 뼈를 가루로 만들어 버린 일권이 지면을 강타했다.
198|
199|동시에 하늘이 쪼개지는 듯한 굉음과 함께 거대한 구덩이가 패었다.
200|
201|오싹.
202|
203|동천마군은 전신의 솜털이 곤두서는 듯한 감각을 느꼈다.
204|
205|과연 자신이 평범한 인간처럼 통증을 느꼈다면, 그렇게 지금의 적천강과 맞섰다면 과연 얼마나 버틸 수 있었을까.
206|
207|도대체 몇 번째 죽음을 맞이했을까.
208|
209|‘이건.’
210|
211|스스로 불사의 존재라고 여겼다. 이미 오래전 사라져 버린 무신이 아닌 이상, 그 누가 온다 해도 쓰러트릴 자신이 있었다.
212|
213|하지만 아니었다.
214|
215|‘피하지 못하면, 죽는다.’
216|
217|동천마군은 살고 싶었다.
218|
219|이미 한 번 죽은 몸이라 해도 이 삶을 이어 가고 싶었다.
220|
221|적어도 증오스러운 피를 이어받은 황실과, 태조의 업적이자 유산인 이 대국을 허물어트려야 했다.
222|
223|복수가 끝날 때까지, 그는 쓰러질 수 없었다.
224|
225|처참한 죽음을 맞이한 가족과 사문의 사람들.
226|
227|그리고 이날만을 위해 괴물이 되기를 선택한 동천마군 자신을 위해서라도.
228|
229|‘난. 나는…….’
230|
231|으득.
232|
233|동천마군은 이를 악물었다. 더는 남아 있지 않은 핏물 대신 살점이 떨어져 나갔다.
234|
235|‘결코 쓰러질 수 없다.’
236|
237|동천마군 스스로도 알 수 없었다.
238|
239|그것이 지금까지 이어진 분노인지. 복수에 대한 집념인지.
240|
241|아니면 일생일대의 대적(大敵)을 맞닥트린 무인이 발휘한 마지막 투혼인지.
242|
243|다만 한 가지는 확실했다.
244|
245|앞서 적천강이 그러했듯이 동천마군 역시 기존의 한계를 넘어섰다는 것.
246|
247|슈확!
248|
249|찰나의 순간. 벼락처럼 공간을 가로지른 지풍(指風)이 적천강의 목을 관통했다.
250|
251|아니, 관통한 것처럼 보였다.
252|
253|연신 물러서는 동천마군을 향해 한 줄기 불꽃이 되어 들이닥치던 적천강의 신형이, 관통당한 목에서 피를 흩뿌리며 쓰러져야 할 그의 모습이 아지랑이처럼 흐트러지기 전까지는.
254|
255|“……!”
256|
257|이형환위(移形換位).
258|
259|그 네 글자가 섬광이 되어 뇌리를 스친 순간, 동천마군은 뒤로 돌아섬과 동시에 하나밖에 남지 않은 팔에 들린 요령을 휘둘렀다.
260|
261|후웅!
262|
263|세찬 파공성과 함께 내리그어지는 요령이 사기를 머금고 빛난다.
264|
265|단 일격. 일격이라도 제대로 적중시킨다면 그 누구라 해도 온전할 수 없다.
266|
267|그것이 초인이라 불리는 초절정 고수들의 싸움이니까.
268|
269|화왕과 동천마군. 초절정이라는 세 글자로도 그 무위를 온전히 표현할 수 없는 괴물들의 싸움이니까.
270|
271|하지만.
272|
273|콰득.
274|
275|적어도 지금 이 순간, 어쩌면 오늘 이후로 두 번 다시 도달하지 못할 새로운 경지를 맛보고 있는 누군가에게는 아니었다.
276|
277|‘고작 이 정도였더냐.’
278|
279|그건 소리 내어 전해진 육성도, 전음도 아니었다.
280|
281|그러나 동천마군은 똑똑히 들었다. 보았다.
282|
283|화염이 깃든 손으로 요령을 붙잡은 채 자신을 응시하는 적천강의 안광에서, 차갑게 다물린 그의 입가에서 들리지 않는 목소리를.
284|
285|동시에 다음 순간 불길에 휩싸이는 자신의 팔을.
286|
287|화륵, 콰아아!
288|
289|산기슭에 번진 화마(火魔)는 며칠이 지나도 사라지지 않지만, 주인의 의지를 따라 일어난 열양지기는 아니었다.
290|
291|끔찍한 열기를 머금은 그것은 찰나에 시작되어 순식간에 사그라졌다.
292|
293|하나밖에 남지 않았던, 동천마군의 마지막 팔을 흔적도 없이 녹여 버리며.
294|
295|하지만 분노한 스승의 응징은 그것으로 끝난 것이 아니었다.
296|
297|콰직!
298|
299|동천마군의 시야가 흔들렸다.
300|
301|팔이 흔적도 없이 녹아내림과 동시에 옆구리를 후려친 일권이, 살과 뼈마디를 부수는 것으로도 모자라 오래전 썩어 버린 그의 오장육부로 화염을 쏟아붓는 것이 느껴졌다.
302|
303|‘안 돼!’
304|
305|적천강의 일격, 일격을 허용할 때마다 죽음 역시 한 걸음씩 가까워지는 상황.
306|
307|쐐애애액!
308|
309|앞서의 공격으로 상반신의 절반이 새카맣게 그을린 동천마군은 튕겨 나가는 힘을 거스르지 않았다.

All of it had vaporized or turned to ash. It was gone beyond recovery unless time itself could be turned back.

[P89]
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord knew it better than anyone.

[P90]
So did Jeok Cheongang.

[P91]
*Step.*

[P92]
Jeok Cheongang took a single stride, and the space between them folded.

[P93]
Thrown backward like a misfired cannonball, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord gritted his teeth and twisted his body.

[P94]
*Crack. BAM!*

[P95]
A fist grazed his side—if pulverizing a handspan of flesh and bone could be called a graze—and slammed into the ground.

[P96]
A tremendous boom split the sky. A massive crater opened beneath it.

[P97]
A chill ran through the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord. He felt as though every hair on his body stood on end.

[P98]
If he felt pain like an ordinary human, how long could he have lasted against Jeok Cheongang as he was now?

[P99]
How many times would he have died?

[P100]
*This is…*

[P101]
He had believed himself immortal. With the Martial God long gone, he had been confident that no one could bring him down.

[P102]
He had been wrong.

[P103]
*If I can’t dodge, I’ll die.*

[P104]
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord wanted to live.

[P105]
Even if he had died once already, he wanted this life to continue.

[P106]
At the very least, he had to bring down the Imperial House, heir to that loathsome bloodline, and the Great Nation that was Taizu’s achievement and legacy.

[P107]
He could not fall before his revenge was complete.

[P108]
For his family and the members of his sect, who had met such horrific deaths.

[P109]
And for himself—the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, who had chosen to become a monster for the sake of this day.

[P110]
*I. I…*

[P111]
*Grind.*

[P112]
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord clenched his teeth. With no blood left to spill, bits of flesh fell away instead.

[P113]
*I cannot fall.*

[P114]
He himself could not have said what drove him.

[P115]
Was it the rage that had sustained him all this time? His determination to take revenge?

[P116]
Or the last surge of fighting spirit from a martial artist facing the greatest enemy of his life?

[P117]
Only one thing was certain.

[P118]
Just as Jeok Cheongang had before him, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had surpassed his former limits.

[P119]
*Whoosh!*

[P120]
In the blink of an eye, Finger Qi streaked across the space between them like lightning and pierced Jeok Cheongang’s neck.

[P121]
No. It only appeared to.

[P122]
Jeok Cheongang had been charging at him like a streak of flame. For an instant, it seemed he would fall with blood spraying from his pierced neck—then his figure dissolved like a heat haze.

[P123]
“……!”

[P124]
*Shifting Form and Position.*

[P125]
The four characters flashed through the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s mind. He spun around and swung the bell held in his only remaining hand.

[P126]
*Whoosh!*

[P127]
The bell slashed downward with a fierce whistle, gleaming with death energy.

[P128]
One blow. If even one strike landed cleanly, no one would escape unscathed.

[P129]
That was how battles between Supreme Peak masters called superhuman were fought.

[P130]
And the Fire King and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord were monsters whose martial prowess could not be fully expressed even by the words *Supreme Peak*.

[P131]
But—

[P132]
*Crack.*

[P133]
That strike was not enough against someone who, for this moment at least, had reached a new realm. One he might never reach again, even if he lived past today.

[P134]
*Was that all you had?*

[P135]
Jeok Cheongang had neither spoken aloud nor used Sound Transmission.

[P136]
Yet the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord heard him clearly. He saw the unheard words in Jeok Cheongang’s gaze as he gripped the bell with a flame-wreathed hand, in his tightly closed lips.

[P137]
Then he saw his own arm catch fire.

[P138]
*Fwoosh! KABOOOOOM!*

[P139]
A wildfire on a mountainside might burn for days. The Scorching Yang Qi summoned by its master’s will did not.

[P140]
Its dreadful heat flared in an instant and faded just as quickly, melting away the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s last arm without a trace.

[P141]
But the enraged Master’s punishment did not end there.

[P142]
*CRACK!*

[P143]
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s vision shook.

[P144]
As his arm vanished, a fist smashed into his side. It crushed flesh and bone, then poured flames into his organs, long since rotted away.

[P145]
*No!*

[P146]
Each blow Jeok Cheongang landed brought death another step closer.

[P147]
*SHWAAAA!*

[P148]
Half the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s upper body had been scorched black by that last attack. He did not resist the force hurling him backward.

[P149]
Instead, he poured every bit of energy remaining into his still-intact legs.

[P150]
He had lost both arms and the bell. He had to put as much distance between them as he could.

[P151]
He kicked off the ground with all his strength—and felt a grip of immense force seize his ankle.

[P152]
*Crack.*

[P153]
Flesh was crushed. Bone shattered.

[P154]
And at the same time—

[P155]
*Whoooosh!*

[P156]
The world turned upside down. Through the rushing wind, the ground surged up to meet him.

[P157]
*KABOOOOOM!*

[P158]
A thunderous impact left his ears ringing, and the ground heaved upward.

[P159]
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord lay buried deep amid shattered dirt and rock, in earth that had hardened like granite. His eyelids trembled.

[P160]
*This is…*

[P161]
For well over half a century, he had worked in the shadows of the Imperial Palace and seen countless Supreme Peak masters.

[P162]
So he knew.

[P163]
This was not a question of speed or strength alone.

[P164]
Jeok Cheongang now stood in a realm beyond his.

[P165]
*Rumble.*

[P166]
He felt not the slightest pain. That made the sensation all the clearer.

[P167]
One of his two remaining legs had just been torn off.

[P168]
And that meant only one thing.

[P169]
*There’s nowhere left to retreat.*

[P170]
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord gave a hollow laugh.

[P171]
Was that the smile of a man finally accepting the death before him?

[P172]
No.

[P173]
It was the bitter laugh of a man forced to choose between the revenge he had awaited so long and his life. He had decided to reveal the blade he had kept hidden to draw at the very end.

[P174]
—Come out, Heaven’s Slaughter.

[P175]
The faint Sound Transmission slipped between his moving lips, its meaning unclear.

[P176]
*Shiver.*

[P177]
The empty air wavered.

[P178]
An assassin dropped through the drifting ash and embers. The old man, whose limp gave no hint of his speed, shot forward like a flash of light and slashed a dagger down at the crown of Jeok Cheongang’s head.

[P179]
*Whoosh!*

[P180]
The ambush was nearly perfect. No—it was perfect beyond dispute.

[P181]
Just as it was about to succeed—

[P182]
*SHWAAAA!*

[P183]
A spear cut through space like a streak of flame.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P108]
For his family and the members of his sect, who had met such horrific deaths.

[P109]
And for himself—the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, who had chosen to become a monster for the sake of this day.

[P110]
*I. I…*

[P111]
*Grind.*

[P112]
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord clenched his teeth. With no blood left to spill, bits of flesh fell away instead.

[P113]
*I cannot fall.*

[P114]
He himself could not have said what drove him.

[P115]
Was it the rage that had sustained him all this time? His determination to take revenge?

[P116]
Or the last surge of fighting spirit from a martial artist facing the greatest enemy of his life?

[P117]
Only one thing was certain.

[P118]
Just as Jeok Cheongang had before him, the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord had surpassed his former limits.

[P119]
*Whoosh!*

[P120]
In the blink of an eye, Finger Qi streaked across the space between them like lightning and pierced Jeok Cheongang’s neck.

[P121]
No. It only appeared to.

[P122]
Jeok Cheongang had been charging at him like a streak of flame. For an instant, it seemed he would fall with blood spraying from his pierced neck—then his figure dissolved like a heat haze.

[P123]
“……!”

[P124]
*Shifting Form and Position.*

[P125]
The four characters flashed through the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s mind. He spun around and swung the bell held in his only remaining hand.

[P126]
*Whoosh!*

[P127]
The bell slashed downward with a fierce whistle, gleaming with death energy.

[P128]
One blow. If even one strike landed cleanly, no one would escape unscathed.

[P129]
That was how battles between Supreme Peak masters called superhuman were fought.

[P130]
And the Fire King and the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord were monsters whose martial prowess could not be fully expressed even by the words *Supreme Peak*.

[P131]
But—

[P132]
*Crack.*

[P133]
That strike was not enough against someone who, for this moment at least, had reached a new realm. One he might never reach again, even if he lived past today.

[P134]
*Was that all you had?*

[P135]
Jeok Cheongang had neither spoken aloud nor used Sound Transmission.

[P136]
Yet the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord heard him clearly. He saw the unheard words in Jeok Cheongang’s gaze as he gripped the bell with a flame-wreathed hand, in his tightly closed lips.

[P137]
Then he saw his own arm catch fire.

[P138]
*Fwoosh! KABOOOOOM!*

[P139]
A wildfire on a mountainside might burn for days. The Scorching Yang Qi summoned by its master’s will did not.

[P140]
Its dreadful heat flared in an instant and faded just as quickly, melting away the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s last arm without a trace.

[P141]
But the enraged Master’s punishment did not end there.

[P142]
*CRACK!*

[P143]
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s vision shook.

[P144]
As his arm vanished, a fist smashed into his side. It crushed flesh and bone, then poured flames into his organs, long since rotted away.

[P145]
*No!*

[P146]
Each blow Jeok Cheongang landed brought death another step closer.

[P147]
*SHWAAAA!*

[P148]
Half the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s upper body had been scorched black by that last attack. He did not resist the force hurling him backward.

[P149]
Instead, he poured every bit of energy remaining into his still-intact legs.

[P150]
He had lost both arms and the bell. He had to put as much distance between them as he could.

[P151]
He kicked off the ground with all his strength—and felt a grip of immense force seize his ankle.

[P152]
*Crack.*

[P153]
Flesh was crushed. Bone shattered.

[P154]
And at the same time—

[P155]
*Whoooosh!*

[P156]
The world turned upside down. Through the rushing wind, the ground surged up to meet him.

[P157]
*KABOOOOOM!*

[P158]
A thunderous impact left his ears ringing, and the ground heaved upward.

[P159]
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord lay buried deep amid shattered dirt and rock, in earth that had hardened like granite. His eyelids trembled.

[P160]
*This is…*

[P161]
For well over half a century, he had worked in the shadows of the Imperial Palace and seen countless Supreme Peak masters.

[P162]
So he knew.

[P163]
This was not a question of speed or strength alone.

[P164]
Jeok Cheongang now stood in a realm beyond his.

[P165]
*Rumble.*

[P166]
He felt not the slightest pain. That made the sensation all the clearer.

[P167]
One of his two remaining legs had just been torn off.

[P168]
And that meant only one thing.

[P169]
*There’s nowhere left to retreat.*

[P170]
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord gave a hollow laugh.

[P171]
Was that the smile of a man finally accepting the death before him?

[P172]
No.

[P173]
It was the bitter laugh of a man forced to choose between the revenge he had awaited so long and his life. He had decided to reveal the blade he had kept hidden to draw at the very end.

[P174]
—Come out, Heaven’s Slaughter.

[P175]
The faint Sound Transmission slipped between his moving lips, its meaning unclear.

[P176]
*Shiver.*

[P177]
The empty air wavered.

[P178]
An assassin dropped through the drifting ash and embers. The old man, whose limp gave no hint of his speed, shot forward like a flash of light and slashed a dagger down at the crown of Jeok Cheongang’s head.

[P179]
*Whoosh!*

[P180]
The ambush was nearly perfect. No—it was perfect beyond dispute.

[P181]
Just as it was about to succeed—

[P182]
*SHWAAAA!*

[P183]
A spear cut through space like a streak of flame.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. - a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.
